1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons, __the weapons stores processor panel further comprising a control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position, wherein when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and enables generation of the fire signals, when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to the weapons interface controller and prevents generation of the fire signals, and when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to the weapons interface controller and prevents generation of the fire signals.__

2. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons interface includes a first weapons interface to a first weapon and a second weapons interface to a second weapon, the first weapon and the second weapon being of different types, __and wherein the control panel further includes a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals to the weapons interface.__

3. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 2 wherein: the weapons interface includes a third weapons interface to a third weapon and a fourth weapons interface to a fourth weapon, the third weapon and the fourth weapon being of different types.

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel communicates with the weapons interface using a MIL-STD-1760 standard, __and wherein the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system, when an override switch is in a manual override position.__

5. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel.

6. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a data concentrator unit that conditions outputs from the flight management system for display on a multi-function display, __wherein the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, a control display unit, and the multi-function display.__

7. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: PA-0016231-US 7 a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position.

8. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the master arm position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel enables generation of the fire signals.

9. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the safe position, the weapons stores processor panel provides power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

10. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: when the master arm switch is in the off position, the weapons stores processor panel disables power to a weapons interface controller and the weapons stores processor panel prevents generation of the fire signals.

11. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel.

12. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a override switch for having a weight-on-wheels (WOW) position and a manual override position.

13. (Previously presented) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 12 wherein: when the override switch is in the manual override position, the weapons stores processor panel commands the weapons interface directly, without reliance on the flight management system.

14. (Previously presented) PA-0016231-US 8 14. The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals to the weapons interface.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction function display, __and wherein the weapons stores processor panel provides data for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons.__

16. (Cancelled)

17.
